Integrity: Trustworthy (R_net: 1.5, Uncertainty z: 0)
Zelensky offered dismissed Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov a Deputy PM post for military innovation. Fedorov publicly declined, stating he will accept no post other than Defense Minister.

The Bright Side:
By refusing a symbolic promotion, Fedorov exposes the toothless nature of secondary cabinet positions and demands real authority to fight corruption.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The stated reason is institutional capability (WHAT), but the underlying dynamic is a struggle for executive control (WHO) between reformists and military command.

Social Physics Analysis:
Fedorov leverages public support and his team's reform record to resist political sidelining, refusing a compromise that would dilute his power to enact structural changes.

The Trajectory: The Path of Redemption.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Good. The action forces a focus on real systemic authority.

The Unavoidable Truth: Symbolic government roles often lack the actual power to enact deep systemic reforms.

The Unavoidable Lie: That accepting a lesser post would allow his team to continue their work effectively.

Alethekanon:
Fedorov's refusal is a calculated move. Accepting a deputy PM role would co-opt his reformist brand without giving him the authority to execute his plans. It is a rational defense of his political capital.

Awwthekanon:
It takes immense courage to stand up for your team's mission and refuse a comfortable title when you know it won't let you truly help protect your country and fight corruption.
